text:
Sam: Customer hit a hard error when using JSON-mode strict for structured output. They get a 415 and we can't repro locally.
Sam: Repro steps they sent (simplified):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -d '{"prompt":"give me json","response_format":"json","strict":true}'
```
Sam: Response from our API: HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
{"error":"unsupported content-type: expected application/json when response_format=json and strict=true"}
Raj: Hmm - looks like a content-type mismatch. But 415 shouldn't happen if our docs accept charset differences. Did the customer include an Accept header? Any proxy rewriting headers?
Sam: They included no Accept header (fetch default). They said they're using a third-party gateway that rewrites Content-Type to `text/plain; charset=utf-8` when forwarding.
Raj: That matches. When strict mode is enabled we perform exact header checks: Content-Type must start with `application/json` and Accept must include `application/json` (or be absent if using legacy permissive mode). If proxy changes to `text/plain` we return 415.
Sam: Customer insists it worked yesterday. Could be a rollout or our strict-mode flag being enforced on their org. Can we check config for their org id 12345? 
emily: I can check feature flags and recent deploys. Also check edge logs for that org to see effective headers. Can you paste the raw X-Forwarded-* headers from the request?
Sam: I asked customer for the full raw request; they pasted this snippet: 
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
X-Forwarded-For: 34.12.2.9
User-Agent: ExampleClient/1.2

{"prompt":"give me json","response_format":"json","strict":true}
```
Sam: They also said they upgraded their SDK from 0.9.x -> 1.1.0 which changes default Content-Type.
Raj: Two hypotheses: 1) SDK change set Content-Type to text/plain, exposing upstream proxy behavior; 2) we enabled stricter header enforcement for structured output on their org during a canary.
support-bot: INCIDENT CHECK: no active global rollout for "strict-json-enforcement". Last canary toggled on 2026-02-28 for 10% of orgs.
emily: I pulled edge logs for org 12345 between 2026-03-11T09:00 and 09:30. I see requests from their IP with Content-Type `text/plain; charset=utf-8` getting 415. No evidence our canary flagged them. Looks like an upstream change.
Sam: Customer is blocked — they have thousands of requests failing and billing alarms firing. They want a mitigation.
Raj: Short-term mitigation options: 
- Ask customer to force `Content-Type: application/json` in their SDK/fetch call. Example: `fetch(url, {headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json'}})`
- Or we can add a temporary compatibility layer: accept `text/plain` payloads when `response_format=json` if body parses as JSON and `X-Allow-Compat: true` present.
Sam: Customer can't change proxy quickly. They asked if we can whitelist their org to be permissive.
emily: I can enable a per-org compatibility flag. It requires a config change and deploy but it's low-risk. I'll coordinate with infra for a quick toggle.
Raj: Before toggling, capture a failing raw request and full response with trace id. Need to ensure we don't open a path that could be abused (e.g., receiving non-JSON content and treating it as JSON). Only enable for org 12345 and log parsing failures as errors.
Sam: Trace id they provided: trace-0a1b2c3d. Paste of server response earlier includes that id? They have it in the headers when they captured it.
support-bot: ACTION LOGGED: create support-runbook task #SR-6721 for org 12345; assign to emily and raj; priority: high.
emily: I'll open a deploy rollback path and enable the compat flag for org 12345 now. Will post when done.
Sam: Customer replied — they can do a temporary client change (set Accept) but won't be able to push the Content-Type change for 24 hours. If we can accept requests that have `Accept: application/json` even if Content-Type is text/plain, that might be safest.
Raj: Ok plan: emily enables per-org compatibility toggle that relaxes Content-Type check if `Accept: application/json` present AND body parses as JSON. We add a metric/alert for parsing failures. Also add a follow-up to require customers to set proper headers and update SDK docs.
emily: Toggle enabled for org 12345 at 1790122401. Edge logs show subsequent requests with Accept header now returning 200.
Sam: Customer confirms traffic recovered. They've paused billing alarms. They also requested a postmortem and a doc update for the SDK change.
Raj: I'll own the doc update and add a snippet to the SDK changelog explaining Content-Type/Accept expectations and how strict mode behaves.
Sam: Thanks everyone. Closing once postmortem is done.
support-bot: THREAD CLOSED: closed by sam at 1790122454
